In the middle distance, the original desk rises as a weathered platform on bent graphite legs, its phone a slumped mound. Nothing is ringing. In the foreground, a slim graphite line-laying rig on a narrow wheeled chassis unspools a single acid-lime cable across the plain, running from one handset it has lifted and set upright back to the old desk.

title: Save the shop
hero: shop counter with till
start: A small shop counter of brushed graphite, about the size of a shoebox, stands at the centre of a pale neutral tabletop, its frosted glass display front softly glowing from within. On top sits a compact till: a graphite body, blank frosted acrylic keys and a closed cash drawer. Beside the till, one ivory envelope with a blank label leans against a small graphite bell, its flap closed with an acid-lime seal that marks it as the rent notice. Behind the counter, a short graphite shelf holds a few ivory card boxes of stock. A folded ivory apron hangs from a hook at one end of the counter. Light dust lies along the till's keys and the shelf edge.
end: The same counter is sinking. Plain-sealed ivory envelopes have piled onto it in a slumping mound that buries the till up to its keys and spills over both ends. The counter's graphite legs have buckled, and it sags into the tabletop at one corner, the frosted display front cracked diagonally. Envelopes are frozen mid-slide off the mound, fanning out across the floor toward the viewer. The cash drawer has sprung open, empty. The original envelope with the acid-lime seal sits near the bottom of the pile, pressed flat. The stock shelf behind leans forward, one box caught mid-fall. The bell lies on its side, and the apron has slipped from its hook.
apocalypse: A low hill of weathered ivory envelopes rolls away to a quiet horizon, layered and fused into pale strata like old snowpack. At its heart sits the shop, now the size of a small building, sunk to its roofline: the graphite counter is a cracked lintel and the till a slumped boulder of blank keys. A graphite roller shutter, pitted and dented, has come down across the whole front. In the foreground, a slim graphite unlocking rig on a jointed arm reaches up and turns an acid-lime key in the shutter's lock, while a pair of graphite winches on either side have started to lift the shutter, revealing a strip of soft frosted light from inside. Loose envelopes slide down the slopes.

title: Box on the way out
hero: ivory card box of desk belongings
start: An empty ivory card box, about the size of a shoebox, sits open at the centre of a pale graphite desk on a neutral tabletop, its flaps folded out and creased crisp. Around it the desk is still set up: a frosted glass mug, a small graphite desk lamp, a framed ivory card photo turned away with a blank back, and a graphite stapler. In front of the box lies a studio access badge, a frosted acrylic card with a blank front, on a neatly coiled acid-lime lanyard. Behind the desk, a long corridor begins as a strip of pale floor running away between low graphite walls. Dust sits in the stapler's hinge, and the box corners show faint scuffs.
end: The same box is now packed and overfull, its flaps forced upright: the mug, the lamp with its cord trailing out, the stapler and the frame are jammed inside at angles. It rides on a slim graphite push trolley rolling away down the long corridor, frozen mid-motion, wheels blurred and leaving a thin scuff line. Behind it, the stripped desk shows only pale rectangles in the dust where things stood. The frame has slipped from the box and is caught mid-fall, and loose ivory papers flutter out in its wake. The acid-lime lanyard hangs over the box's edge, the badge swinging out on it. The corridor's graphite walls recede in a long, even line.
apocalypse: A long, dim hall of studio ruins stretches away, its roof long gone and the sky pale overhead. Tall graphite lighting gantries stand bent and half fallen, and sheets of ivory card backdrop hang torn from their frames in deep folds. The floor is a drift of dust and fallen flats, and the old corridor runs through it as a cracked causeway. At its far end sits the box, now the size of a cottage, weathered and sagging, flaps curled open, the lamp's shade jutting out like a chimney. From a slim graphite tripod crane in the foreground, an acid-lime spotlight throws a clean circle of light onto the box, while the crane's graphite hook lowers toward it to lift it free.

title: Temp supply mystery
hero: stocked office supply shelf
start: A graphite supply shelf, about the height of a cereal box, stands at the right of a pale neutral tabletop, its three levels neatly stocked with ivory card notepads, a row of graphite staplers, tape in frosted acrylic dispensers and small boxes of clips. At the left sits a small graphite temp desk, bare except for a single ivory pad and a frosted acrylic visitor badge on an acid-lime clip. A graphite desk lamp is angled down onto the pad. Between the shelf and the temp desk stand two taller graphite desks with shallow drawers, closed. The shelf edges are clean where items were recently straightened, and dust lies only in the back corners.
end: The same supply shelf is half empty, pale dust-free rectangles marking where staplers and pads have vanished, and a few stragglers are frozen mid-slide off the edge. On the two taller desks, the drawers have slammed shut and small graphite padlocks hang from them, still swinging. Every desk lamp in the scene has swivelled on its arm to point at the temp desk, which sits in a hard pool of overlapping light, the acid-lime badge clip glaring in it. Its single pad has been knocked askew. A trail of paper clips runs across the tabletop from the shelf, not to the temp desk, but into the gap behind one locked drawer.
apocalypse: A long warehouse aisle runs to a vanishing point, lined on both sides with toppled graphite shelving the size of apartment blocks, their levels bare and furred with grey-ivory dust that has settled into rippled drifts across the floor. Desk lamps as tall as streetlights lean over the aisle, shades cracked. The small temp desk stands intact beneath them, its badge long faded. In the midground, a slim graphite inventory rig rolls down the centre on a single rail, sweeping an acid-lime scanning bar across the shelves. It has stopped beside a buried desk drawer the size of a shipping container, now pried open to reveal a neat hidden stash of staplers, pads and clips. Dust eddies in the rig's wake.

title: Plaque race
hero: empty wall-plaque frame
start: A long miniature store aisle runs away from the viewer down the centre of a pale neutral tabletop, flanked by two low graphite shelving units stocked with neat rows of ivory card boxes and frosted acrylic jars. At the far end, on a graphite end wall, hangs one empty plaque frame, a rectangle of brushed graphite with an acid-lime backing card and nothing mounted on it. A single graphite wire shopping cart, about the size of a matchbox, is parked at the near end pointing down the aisle. The floor tiles carry faint scuffs. The shelves are faced perfectly, and a fine line of dust runs along the lowest shelf lip.
end: The same aisle has become a racetrack. Several graphite carts are frozen mid-charge down it, wheels blurred and splayed, one tipped onto two wheels, another rammed into a shelf. Their wakes have swept stock off both sides: ivory boxes tumble in mid-air, jars roll and bounce, and one shelf leans inward, shedding its contents in a slide. At the end wall, the acid-lime frame is now surrounded by a spreading grid of more empty plain graphite frames, crowding up and outward toward the ceiling, several hanging crooked. Skid marks on the floor tiles run straight back to the near end of the aisle, where the first cart stood.
apocalypse: A long canyon of collapsed shelving stretches toward a pale horizon, the shelves now as big as office towers, fallen inward against each other to form a jagged arch overhead. The floor is a sediment of crushed ivory boxes and frosted acrylic fragments drifted into banks. Dented graphite carts the size of trucks lie on their sides, wheels in the air, half buried. The end wall still stands far off, its grid of empty frames hanging askew and bleached. In the foreground, one slim graphite cart rig with acid-lime wheels rolls clear of the debris along a newly laid graphite track, carrying the original plaque frame upright on its bed, its backing faded. Dust settles slowly behind it.

title: Pudding loophole
hero: frosted dessert cup with coupon
start: A single dessert cup, about the size of a shot glass, stands on a brushed graphite stockroom shelf that runs across the back of a pale neutral tabletop. The cup is frosted acrylic with a milky glow, sealed with a crisp ivory paper lid pressed flat at the rim. Beside it, clipped to the shelf edge by a small graphite clip, hangs one coupon of ivory card with deckled perforated edges, a blank front and a thin acid-lime stripe along its top border. The rest of the shelf is empty. Below, a folded ivory delivery slip and a graphite box cutter lie on the tabletop. Fine dust sits along the shelf lip.
end: The same shelf now sags under towers of identical frosted cups, stacked in pyramids and columns up to the top of the frame. The shelf has bowed in the middle, and cups slide off it in a frozen cascade, rolling across the tabletop in a flood that pours toward the front edge, out toward unseen warehouse aisles. The coupon hangs at a steep angle from its clip, its acid-lime stripe still visible, and a long ribbon of plain clipped coupons now trails from it down to the floor. Delivery slips have piled into a drift, and several paper lids have popped off and hang mid-air. The box cutter is buried under the cups.
apocalypse: A vast warehouse ruin opens under a broken graphite roof, pale sky showing through the gaps. Its floor has become dunes of frosted cups, each now the size of a car, drifted in rippling banks against toppled racking, lids peeled and bleached, some cracked and filled with pale grit. The old aisles show as troughs between the dunes, running to a hazy back wall. The stockroom shelf juts out of the nearest dune as a bent girder, its faded coupon still clipped on. In the foreground, a low, slim graphite pallet rig with acid-lime forks pulls out from under a dune, carrying one tidy pallet of cups stacked square and strapped with ivory card bands along a cleared lane toward an open loading door.

title: Honesty in the meeting
hero: graphite meeting table with agenda
start: A polished oval meeting table of brushed graphite, about the size of a serving tray, fills the centre of a pale neutral tabletop, its surface softly reflecting the light. Six small graphite chairs are tucked in evenly around it. At the head of the table lies one ivory agenda sheet, crisp and square with blank lines, and on it rests a slim graphite pen with an acid-lime cap. In the middle stands a frosted glass water carafe with six empty frosted glasses. A folded ivory card name tent with a blank front sits at each seat. The polish shows only one tiny scuff near the head of the table, and a faint dust haze lies on the chair backs.
end: The same table has been jolted. The agenda sheet is torn cleanly across the middle, the two halves lifting apart in mid-air, and the acid-lime-capped pen is frozen mid-spin above the tear. From the head of the table, the disruption runs outward: name tents have flipped and slide off the edges, the carafe has tipped and its water arcs out in a sheet across the table, glasses topple in a chain, and papers skid toward the far end. Chairs have rolled back on their casters, some turned sideways, one tipping over backward. Water droplets and paper corners trace a clear line back to the torn agenda at the head.
apocalypse: A wide, dim plain of cracked polished stone stretches to a low horizon, and across it lies the meeting table, now the size of a runway, split lengthwise into two tilted slabs with a deep ravine between them. Old water has dried into pale rings on its surface. The chairs, big as houses, lie scattered and overturned, casters in the air, some half buried in drifts of torn ivory paper. The frosted carafe lies shattered in a fan of fragments. In the foreground, a slim graphite lifting rig running on paired rails has righted one chair at the head of the split table and braces it upright with acid-lime struts, set square to the table's end. Fine grit drifts across the slabs.

title: Eight-to-noon window
hero: wall clock with promised arc
start: A round wall clock, about the size of a saucer, hangs on a pale graphite wall panel at the upper left of the frame. It has a brushed graphite rim, a frosted glass front with a plain dial with tick marks, slim graphite pointers, and a thin acid-lime arc painted along one third of the dial, marking the promised service window. To the right, a small front door of ivory card with a graphite knob stands closed in a graphite frame. Below the clock, one ivory card chair waits beside the door, a folded jacket over its back and a cold frosted mug on the floor beside it. Dust sits along the threshold. The pointers rest just inside the start of the arc.
end: The same clock now shows its pointers swept far past the acid-lime arc, the minute pointer frozen mid-blur as it spins around again. The front door is still shut, its knob untouched and dusty. Where one chair stood, a long queue of identical ivory card chairs stretches from the door down a hallway that recedes toward the back of the frame, each with a cold mug beside it, the nearest chairs tipping as the line compresses. The folded jacket has slipped to the floor. Loose blank ivory pages have slid off one seat and fan out in mid-air. A trail of knocked-over mugs leads back along the queue to the door.
apocalypse: A long, roofless hallway runs to a distant point, its graphite walls cracked and leaning, the floor carpeted with drifts of pale dust and fallen ivory card. Chairs the size of cottages line both sides in a broken queue, many tipped over, some half sunk. Across the hallway lies the wall clock, now enormous, fallen flat on its back like a crater rim, its frosted front shattered and its pointers bent upward, the old painted arc faded to grey. At the hallway's end stands the front door, tall as a tower. In the foreground, a slim graphite winch rig on tracks has fixed an acid-lime cable to the door's knob and is hauling it open, a wedge of clean light falling across the dust.

title: Auto-layoff machine
hero: automated desk evaluation box
start: A row of five small office desks, each about the size of a matchbox, lines up across a pale neutral tabletop on a pair of slim graphite rails set flush into the surface. Each desk is brushed graphite with an ivory card top, a tidy stack of ivory papers and a pushed-in chair. On each desk sits a slim graphite evaluation box the size of a sugar cube, with a frosted acrylic window and a small flag arm folded down. Only the box on the middle desk has its acid-lime flag arm lifted, halfway up. At the right end of the rails, a short graphite ramp slopes down to the table edge. Fine dust lies in the rail grooves.
end: The same row is mid-ejection. The evaluation boxes are flagging desks automatically, flag arms rising one after another, and flagged desks are frozen shooting sideways along the rails, papers lifting off their tops in sheets, chairs tipping backward off them. The middle desk with the acid-lime flag leads the way, already launched off the ramp and caught in mid-air past the table edge, its box still attached. Two more desks follow close behind, grinding on the rails in bursts of metal dust. Gaps open in the row where desks stood, and the remaining boxes are just raising their plain graphite flags. Papers drift in a trail back along the rails.
apocalypse: A wide plain of dry ivory grass spreads under a pale horizon, scattered with ejected desks the size of houses lying where they landed: upturned, sunk on one corner, split open with papers spilling into the grass. Deep gouges run from each desk back toward the centre, where a burnt-out evaluation box, now the size of a control bunker, sits scorched dull grey, its frosted window cracked and its flag arms seized. The old rails radiate outward, bent and broken. In the midground, a slim graphite rail-laying rig with acid-lime tongs has placed one fresh straight pair of rails and is setting a single desk back onto them, square and level, the start of a restored row.

title: Stock goes to zero
hero: executive desk stock gauge
start: A round desk gauge, about the size of a saucer, stands on a short graphite pedestal at the centre of a large brushed graphite executive desk on a pale neutral tabletop. It has a frosted glass front with a plain dial with tick marks and a slim acid-lime needle pointing high toward the right of the scale. Around it the office is fully furnished in miniature: a tall-backed chair, a graphite floor lamp glowing through a frosted acrylic shade, a low cabinet of ivory card files, and a framed blank ivory picture on the wall behind. A folded unprinted ivory paper lies beside the gauge. Everything is polished, settled and dust-free.
end: The same gauge now shows its acid-lime needle dropped hard to the far left, frozen mid-bounce against the stop. Around it the office is being emptied in motion: the chair rolls away backward toward the right edge, the cabinet has been tipped onto a graphite dolly with files spilling from open drawers, and the frame on the wall has come down and is caught mid-fall. The floor lamp is switched off, its frosted shade dark. A second lamp is already gone, leaving a pale ring in fresh dust on the floor. Loose ivory files drift across the desk, now bare except for the gauge and the folded paper, and scrape marks trail toward the door.
apocalypse: A vast empty office ruin opens into a dim plateau, its walls fallen outward to leave only a floor slab of cracked graphite panels stretching to the horizon, marked with pale ghost rectangles where furniture once stood. Drifts of ivory files have blown into the corners and lie in wind-shaped banks. Near the centre, the executive desk has collapsed onto one side, and the gauge lies on the floor beside it, now as big as a satellite dish, its frosted front crazed and its old needle bent flat at the bottom of the scale. A slim graphite tripod rig stands over it and, with a fine acid-lime lever arm, lifts a new needle off the stop, just starting to rise. Dust sifts across the floor.

title: Unpaid internship
hero: heavy graphite equipment case
start: A plain bus stop shelter of brushed graphite and frosted glass, about the height of a mug, stands at the left of a pale neutral tabletop. Under its bench, a slim ivory card briefcase with graphite clasps rests upright beside a heavy equipment case: a squat graphite box the size of a matchbox with chamfered corners, a stout carrying handle and an acid-lime latch. To the right, a thin strip of ivory card road runs off toward a small cluster of graphite buildings in the background. A folded ivory card jacket lies across the bench. The case has pressed a small dent into the tabletop beneath it, and dust sits along its seams.
end: The same road now stretches across the whole tabletop, looping and winding past a long line of identical bus stop shelters receding into the distance. At each stop the equipment case sits a little bigger and heavier than at the last, and the final one has grown as large as the shelter itself, crushing the bench flat, cracking the frosted glass and sinking into the tabletop in a spray of chips frozen mid-air. The acid-lime latch sits on that last case, straining at its hinge. The briefcase lies toppled and open at one of the middle stops, papers sliding out. Deep drag marks run along the road from stop to stop, back to the first shelter.
apocalypse: A dim city ruin climbs a long hillside at dusk, its graphite buildings roofless and gapped, the streets choked with pale drift and fallen ivory card. The winding road from before is visible as a cracked switchback terraced up the slope, lined with the bent frames of bus shelters. At the foot of the hill sits the equipment case, as big as a warehouse, its handle arching overhead like a bridge, its corners dented and dusty, its latch faded. In the midground, a slim graphite funicular tram on a single steep rail has taken a small intact equipment case aboard its flat car and climbs toward the hilltop, drawn by an acid-lime cable wheel at the summit station.

title: Wiped project memory
hero: envelope of unexplained items
start: A small ivory paper envelope, about the size of a playing card, lies open at the centre of a pale neutral tabletop, its flap unfolded along crisp creases. Laid out in a neat row beside it are its contents: a graphite key, a folded ivory ticket stub with a blank front, a frosted acrylic marble, a small graphite paperclip, a blank ivory card, and a thin acid-lime thread wound around a graphite spool. Behind the row sit an empty graphite desk organiser and a cold frosted mug, left by someone who is not coming back to explain. Nothing shows why these objects belong together. Fibres fray at the envelope's edges, and dust lies in the key's teeth.
end: The same desk is now crowded with unexplained objects. title: Teleprompter runaway

title: Concession overflow

title: Billable hours

title: Cloned yourself

title: Booby-trapped office

title: Square filter, round hole

title: Shifting cube rooms

title: Contract takes your name

In the foreground, a giant graphite desk lies half sunk, and the fountain pen, big as a mast, leans out of the mud. Fog drifts between the stacks. A slim graphite dredging rig on thin stilt legs has cleared the sheets around it and presses a lime polishing wheel against its front, and under the wheel the inlay stripe is glowing clearly again.

title: Denied claims cubicle
hero: graphite rubber stamp in a card cubicle
start: A cramped cubicle made of three ivory card partition walls, each about as tall as a coffee mug with crisp folded edges and graphite trim, stands on a pale neutral tabletop. Inside, a small graphite desk fills most of the floor. On it lies a single ivory claim form with blank boxes, and beside it a graphite rubber stamp with a chamfered body rests on a frosted acrylic ink pad. Stamped forms stack in towering, slanting piles on the desk and spill from the in-tray in a torrent. On the canyon floor, a giant graphite stamp lies on its side with its body cracked, and the ink pad beside it has dried into a split grey crust. The desk is crushed flat beneath a slab of forms, only one corner showing. title: Task board stampede
hero: ivory card task board with frosted tiles
start: A flat game board of ivory card, about the size of a place mat, lies on a pale neutral tabletop, its surface ruled with a winding path of blank squares. Small task tiles of frosted acrylic, each the size of a sugar cube, sit stacked in a neat graphite tray at the board's left end. On the start square rests a single acid-lime token. In the foreground, the giant ivory game board lies torn and curled up like a broken terrace, its path squares faded. The desk is flattened beneath a ridge of tiles, its laptop split open and bleached. A graphite die the size of a building sits embedded in a furrow. In the midground, a slim graphite sorting rig on long spider legs straddles the board, picking tiles from the ruts with a fine clamp and stacking them back in their tray, and its lime pointer arm sets one token squarely back on the start square.

title: Thawed and outdated
inspired_by: Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery (1997)
hero: frosted-glass cryo chamber holding an old computer
start: A tall cryo chamber the size of a wine bottle stands upright at the left of a pale neutral tabletop: a frosted-glass cylinder with a brushed graphite base and cap, its milky walls glowing faintly and misted with frost crystals. Sealed inside, blurred, is a small office desk kit: a boxy old computer with a chunky ivory case and a curved frosted screen, a coiled ivory cord and a graphite keyboard. title: Overqualified at the counter
hero: record-shop counter with turntable and list cards
start: A record-shop counter of brushed graphite metal, about a forearm long, sits across the midground of a pale neutral tabletop. At its left end stands a small turntable with a frosted acrylic platter and a graphite tonearm resting in its cradle, its acid-lime needle cartridge poised but idle. At the right end lies a neat stack of ivory list cards, each blank and slightly curled, squared against a graphite card box. Behind the counter, a low graphite bin holds a row of plain ivory record sleeves standing upright. In front, three frosted-glass shopping baskets wait in a short line, empty. A cold mug sits by the stack. Card edges show fine fibres, and dust rests on the platter.

In front, the line of frosted-glass baskets has grown into a long queue snaking off the left edge, the front baskets heaped with sleeves pulled from the bin and still waiting. In the foreground, the giant graphite counter lies cracked across its middle, half sunk in card drifts. A long line of frosted-glass baskets, each the size of a car, runs off into the distance, tilted and filled with bleached sleeves and fallen cards. The record bin has spilled plain sleeves across the ground like fallen slabs. In the midground, the turntable has been dug out: its frosted platter, cracked and dusty, sits level again, and a slim graphite crane arm on a pivoting base lowers a lime needle cartridge gently onto one clean record on the platter, the first groove catching the light.

title: System erased you
hero: ivory employee file folder and access badge
start: A graphite filing cabinet, about the height of a shoebox on end, stands at the right of a pale neutral tabletop, its top drawer pulled open to show a row of ivory folders with unmarked tabs. On the desk in front of it lies a single thick employee file, an ivory folder with crisp creases, holding a blank photo card and ruled sheets. Beside it rests a graphite ID badge on a coiled frosted acrylic lanyard, its acid-lime access strip glowing softly. To the left, a small graphite doorframe stands closed with a frosted-glass badge reader beside it. A mug with a faint coffee ring sits by the file. The floor is a deep, pale sediment of ivory paper dust, heaped in drifts against the cabinets. In the foreground, a giant doorframe stands shut, its frosted reader cracked, a bleached badge half buried at its foot. A colossal empty folder lies splayed open like a collapsed tent. In the midground, a slim graphite archive rig runs along overhead rails, its lime folder clamp holding one rebuilt ivory file with its sheets restacked, lowering it into the reopened slot of a single cleaned drawer.

title: Daily sample check
hero: graphite entry turnstile with frosted sample reader
start: A sleek entry turnstile about the height of a coffee pot stands on a pale neutral tabletop, its pillar of brushed graphite metal with chamfered edges and a single frosted-glass gate arm. On top of the pillar sits one compact sample reader, a smooth frosted acrylic block with a small recessed slot. Beside the slot, one acid-lime status light waits, lit steady. In front of the turnstile, three graphite ID badges lie in a neat line on a frosted tray, and a folded ivory visitor pass rests beside them. Behind, a pale lobby floor stretches away, empty and clean. A forgotten graphite umbrella leans on the pillar. Fine polish swirls show on the gate arm, and a trace of dust lines the slot.
end: The same turnstile, grown stricter. A second, then a third frosted reader has been bolted onto the pillar with bulky graphite brackets, each stacked higher and leaning, fasteners bristling. The acid-lime status light on the original reader now blinks, and the frosted gate arm is locked shut. In front, the neat line of badges has become a long queue of badges on frosted trays, snaking back across the lobby floor in tight loops, the rearmost trays sliding into each other. A fourth bracket is caught mid-fall, dropping loose bolts. The visitor pass has blown off and flutters in the air, and the umbrella slides down the pillar. Fine grit from fresh drill holes drifts down.
apocalypse: A vast, pale, perfectly flat lobby floor stretches to a clean horizon under even light, almost spotless but long abandoned. At its centre stands the giant turnstile, now a tower of frosted readers bolted one above another, leaning and cracked, its brackets furred with pale dust. The gate arm is fused shut. Around it, the queue of badge trays forms long curving drifts that coil across the floor into the distance, the trays bleached and chipped. Loose bolts lie scattered like gravel. Beside the tower, a slim graphite rail track has been laid, and a low graphite rig on it has just slid a lime gate panel aside, opening one clean passage alongside the readers, its track running straight past them.

title: Midnight reorg
hero: graphite office floor under tall night windows
start: A model office floor about the size of a tray sits on a pale neutral tabletop, its graphite floor plate scored in a fine grid. Four small graphite desks stand in neat rows, each with a frosted acrylic lamp, an ivory paper notepad and a pushed-in chair. Along the back runs a row of tall sandblasted frosted-glass windows showing dark night blue beyond. Two low ivory card partition walls divide the floor. apocalypse: A wide, tangled ruin spreads under a dark sky, built from office floors the size of city blocks, tilted at clashing angles and stacked into jagged terraces that fade toward a dim horizon. Graphite floor plates overlap like broken slabs, desks cling to slopes or hang from edges, and ivory partitions lie jammed between levels. Frosted windows stand in scattered rows, some upright and some front down. In the midground, one level plate has been cleared, and a slim graphite survey rig on thin tripod legs stakes a lime floor-plan line in a crisp rectangle across it, while a graphite gantry sets the first partition wall along that line and bolts its base plate down.

title: Daily re-onboarding
hero: onboarding cassette on a welcome packet
start: A fresh graphite desk sits on a pale neutral tabletop, bare except for a neat onboarding kit: an ivory card welcome packet, thick and crisply folded with a blank cover, and a small cassette with a frosted acrylic shell and graphite spools resting on top. A compact graphite tape player sits to the right, its lid open. A clean frosted acrylic mug stands on the left, beside a coiled graphite lanyard with a blank badge. The chair is tucked in. The stacks lean into each other, and one is sliding off the left edge, packets fanning into the air. Mounds of welcome packets have weathered into sodden, layered dunes, their covers bleached and frayed. In the foreground, a giant graphite tape player sits half buried in wet ivory paper sand, its lid cracked and its edges scoured. A row of identical mugs lies tipped along the tideline like stones. In the midground, a slim graphite spooling rig on two wide wheels crawls along the flats, winding the stray tape onto a clean reel, and its lime ejector tray slides one small cassette free from the player, a single saved note card clipped on top.

title: Photo-note handoff

Across the ground, thousands of faded instant photos drift in shallow banks, their card edges curled and bleached, their images washed to milky blanks. The giant camera lies on its side at the centre, its lens housing cracked and packed with dust. In the midground, a slim graphite sorting rig on a narrow rail picks prints from the drift one by one and pins them to a short line of low graphite stakes, and a thin lime thread spooled from its arm links the stakes in one clear order toward the nearest wall.

title: Seven-day countdown

apocalypse: A deep, terraced quarry drops away below the viewer, its stepped walls built from thousands of compressed ivory folders, spines bleached, curled and split, descending in broad benches toward a shadowed floor. Beyond the far rim, a pale plain runs to a hazy horizon. On the near rim, the giant countdown dial lies cracked and fully dark, half sunk in a drift of task cards. On the quarry floor, the original project folder sits closed, pinned under loose cards. A slim graphite derrick braced on the rim lowers a lime lifting line straight down, its graphite hook clasped around the folder's spine, and the folder is just beginning to rise, shedding a trickle of cards.

title: Office chain reaction
hero: graphite desk fan aimed at a paper stack
start: A small desk fan with a brushed graphite cage and frosted acrylic blades, about the height of a mug, sits at the left of a pale neutral tabletop, aimed to the right. In front of it lies a loose stack of ivory paper, edges slightly misaligned. Next to the stack stands a full frosted mug, then a graphite power strip whose cord runs back to the fan. apocalypse: A long valley stretches toward a hazy horizon, crossed by a line of giant toppled desks and shelves lying one against the next like fallen dominoes, each the size of a building, weathered, cracked and furred with pale dust. Drifts of ivory paper fill the gaps between them. At the near end, the enormous fan lies on its back, its frosted blades cracked. A colossal mug rests on its side, stained grey inside. The chain runs on down the valley, but in the midground the last desk still stands, leaning only slightly, held by a lime stop block that a slim graphite rail tractor has just pushed into place at its base, bracing it against the fall.

title: Golden ticket line
hero: graphite packing conveyor with inspection gate
start: A tabletop packing line about the length of a forearm runs left to right across a pale neutral tabletop. It is a brushed graphite conveyor on four chamfered legs, with a belt of ivory card slats and fine machining marks on the side rails. Neatly wrapped bars in crisp ivory paper ride the belt at even spacing, their folded ends tucked and creased. Wrapped bars crowd the belt edge to edge, ride up onto each other and tumble off both sides, and torn ivory wrappers peel back in curls that flutter above the gate. The inspection gate is buried to its roof in a heap of bars, its frosted window blocked, and the acid-lime stamp has been knocked off its pad and lies tilted on the pile, half covered. The frosted tray at the far end overflows, with bars sliding off it toward the table edge and one caught mid-drop. The apron has slipped off the stool into the spill. Paper shreds, card crumbs and a haze of dust trace the pileup back along the belt to the feed end.
apocalypse: A wide dry valley stretches to a hazy ridge, its floor a cracked riverbed of compacted ivory wrapper paper, layered and bleached like shale. Across it runs the ruin of the packing line, now the size of a viaduct: graphite legs leaning, belt slats snapped and half buried, and the inspection gate standing as a lone arch with its frosted window shattered and silted with paper grit. Mounds of flattened bars form low ridges along the old flow lines, and dried channels wind between them. In the foreground a slim graphite gantry rig on thin rails straddles one short lane of belt. Its lime rollers turn as it lays fresh ivory slats in a clean straight run, and a jointed arm sets a single intact wrapped bar at the start of the rebuilt lane.

title: Frozen clock
hero: graphite-rimmed office wall clock
start: A round office clock the width of a dinner plate stands on a brushed graphite easel at the back of a pale neutral tabletop. Its sandblasted frosted glass front covers a plain ivory dial with tick marks, and its slim graphite pointers rest a hair short of the top, the moment just before leaving time. In front sits a small graphite desk with a chamfered top holding a neat stack of four ivory task cards squared to the edge and a closed graphite slab of a laptop. A jacket hangs over the chair back, ready to go, and a frosted acrylic desk lamp glows softly. A faint film of dust rests on the clock's machined rim.
end: The same clock and desk are held in a thin rime of frost, as if the room itself has stopped. The acid-lime second pointer is stuck mid-sweep just past the top tick, with fine ice crystals bridging it to the dial. Only the task pile has kept going: ivory cards rise from the desk in a leaning tower past the lamp, fresh cards hang mid-air as they drop onto it from above, and a slide of cards has spilled off the right edge, fanning across the floor and banking against the chair legs. apocalypse: A frost-bound plain of packed ivory card flakes, crusted and wind-scoured, stretches under a pale sky to a line of low ice ridges. Rising from it is the clock, now as tall as a water tower, tilted on its snapped graphite easel. Its frosted glass front is cracked in a wide star and packed with snow-like card fibre. The desk below has become a buried plateau, with only its chamfered corner and the lamp's frosted shade breaking the crust. Long drifts of frozen task cards run downwind from it in layered ridges. On the clock rim, a slim graphite climbing rig clamped to the bezel by four spidery legs has fitted a new lime second pointer to the hub, and the pointer has just moved one tick, shedding a thin curtain of frost.

title: Road not taken
hero: forked card path with briefcase and toolbox
start: A miniature path of pressed ivory card, a short span across, runs from the front of a pale neutral tabletop and splits into two lanes at a graphite signpost with two blank arms. At the fork stand a brushed graphite briefcase with chamfered corners and a matte graphite toolbox with a folding lid, set down side by side as if someone paused to choose. Down the left lane sits a tidy stack of ivory report sheets; down the right, a short frosted acrylic workbench holds one half-built ivory card birdhouse. Set into the signpost base is a small acid-lime compass disc whose needle points exactly between the lanes. Fine crease lines mark the card path, and light scuffs dull the briefcase handle.
end: The same fork, now with both lanes choked. On the left, the report sheets have multiplied into a tall stack that has buckled forward, sending sheets sliding back down the path toward the fork. On the right, the workbench is heaped with unfinished card birdhouses, walls half glued and roofs missing, and several are tumbling off its end. The briefcase has burst open and spilled blank folders across the junction, and the toolbox has tipped, scattering small graphite tools into the paper. The signpost leans, and the acid-lime compass needle is caught mid-swing in a blur. The two drifts of debris meet at the fork, and each can be traced back up its own lane. Paper fibres and card dust hang in the air.
apocalypse: A broad valley of layered ivory paper sediment stretches to distant folded card hills, split down the middle by a dry gorge. On either side run the two old paths, now wide roads of cracked card slabs. One is lined with collapsed towers of weathered report sheets like fallen cliffs; the other is scattered with bleached, roofless birdhouse shells the size of barns. At the head of the valley the signpost lies snapped across the gorge, and the briefcase and toolbox sit half buried as grey boulders with their lids jammed open. On the left rim, a slim graphite bridge-laying rig on tracked feet extends a lime truss span over the gorge, and its far end has just touched the right rim, joining the two roads again.

title: Blinking drive
hero: graphite server rack with frosted drive sleds
start: A server rack about the height of a shoebox stands upright near the centre of a pale neutral tabletop. It is a brushed graphite frame with chamfered rails and fine machining marks, holding eight slim drive sleds in two columns, each faced with frosted acrylic. All sit dark except one near the top, where a small acid-lime status light blinks. To the left, a short frosted glass fan housing sits behind a graphite grille; to the right, an ivory card clipboard of blank log sheets lies squared beside a cold mug. end: The same rack is overheating. Every sled now glows milky white through its frosted front, and several have been shoved half out of their bays by the heat, with one tipping mid-fall toward the table. The acid-lime light that started it still blinks at the top, now lost in the glare. Heat shimmer rises above the frame, and the hot draught has lifted the log sheets off the clipboard: they curl and flip upward, one airborne above the mug. The fan housing's glass has fogged and its grille has bowed outward. The graphite cable has pulled taut and dragged the clipboard to the table edge. The top plate is dulled and faintly warped, and the dust on it has been blown into streaks pointing away from the rack.
apocalypse: A long, dim underground hall stretches away between rows of squat graphite pillars toward a faint doorway of light at the far end. Its floor is drifted with grey-ivory paper dust, rippled like a cave floor. The rack lies toppled against one pillar at enormous scale, its frame bowed and its drive sleds jutting out like broken shelves, their frosted fronts crazed and cold. More sleds lie scattered across the floor in half-buried lines, and the old log sheets have fused into brittle drifts along the walls. Beside the rack, a slim graphite tracked carrier with a lime lift fork has just slid one fresh sled into a straightened bay, and a single lime status light on that sled now glows steady, the only light in the hall.

title: Sponsor clutter
hero: small studio set with two chairs
start: A small studio set about the size of a shoebox diorama sits on a pale neutral tabletop. At the back stands a flat backdrop of ivory card with a soft deckled edge, held by two graphite stands. In front are two low graphite chairs angled toward each other and a small frosted acrylic table between them. On the table lies a single ivory contract sheet, folded once and held by an acid-lime paperclip, the one deal that started it all. To the right, a compact graphite camera on a slim tripod is turned toward the chairs, its frosted glass lens dusty. A folded jacket hangs over one chair. The floor is clean apart from a few faint scuffs.

Blank ivory cartons, frosted glass bottles and graphite tins are stacked on both chairs, crammed onto the table and wedged against the backdrop, which is bowing under dozens of unmarked cards pinned across its front. title: Jump-to-conclusions mat

title: Ticket rail overload

title: Clock-tower deadline

Along it stand the stumps of old graphite towers, and the tallest is the clock tower, now the size of a peak, cracked down its facade with its frosted windows long gone and packed with snow-like paper. On a ledge beside the clock, a slim graphite winch rig bolted to the stonework feeds a lime drive gear into the exposed mechanism, and the gear has just engaged: the loose minute pointer has lifted and moved one tick.

title: Airport form loop

The stanchions have become a row of leaning posts trailing frayed card ribbon, and the traveller's suitcase is a half-buried outcrop, lid open and full of drifted paper. A slim graphite gate conveyor on low rollers runs through the old gate, and its lime-edged belt is carrying one ivory form through the rebuilt frame and out the far side for the first time.

title: Supply closet heist

title: Admin-rights ceiling drop

title: Paperwork twister

title: Deadline asteroid

title: Prototype taken for production

title: Monochrome office

title: Harvest quota

title: Citation quota

title: The call you can't leave

title: Hospitality-suite vigil

title: Remote volleyball coworker

title: Fifteen-minute escape hatch

title: Dinner-table buzz

start: A small round dinner table of matte graphite sits on a pale neutral tabletop, set for two. Each place has a frosted glass plate with a neat serving of ivory card food shapes, a folded ivory napkin and slim graphite cutlery. Two sandblasted frosted glass tumblers stand between them. Beside the near plate lies a slim graphite phone slab front down, with a thin acid-lime notification strip along its edge, dark for now. The chair opposite has a jacket over its back. A frosted acrylic candle glows softly at the centre. Fine crumbs and faint fibres rest on the napkins.
end: The same table during a flood of work. The phone is buzzing, frozen mid-jump a finger's width above the table, its acid-lime strip lit along the whole edge. The vibration has walked it across the setting: it has knocked the near tumbler, which is mid-topple with water arcing out. Ivory memo cards have spread from under the phone across both plates, covering the food, and more are frozen falling onto the table. The food shapes have gone flat and grey-edged. The chair opposite is pushed back and empty, its jacket gone. The candle has guttered and leans in its holder. Crumbs and card dust scatter outward from the phone.
apocalypse: A wide tidal flat of wet grey-ivory sediment stretches to a low, misty horizon, streaked with channels of milky water. Rising from it is the dinner table at the size of a plaza, tilted, its graphite top cracked across, both plates broken and filled with silt, and the tumblers lying on their sides like fallen towers. Memo cards have hardened into flat terraces of sediment around the ruin. The phone lies half sunk near the edge like a dark slab. A slim graphite rig on long wading legs has re-laid one clean place setting on a leveled section of the table, and its arm is drawing a lime cloth over the phone.

title: Dial-up handshake
hero: boxy modem on a desk with a phone line
start: A boxy modem about the size of a paperback sits on a small graphite desk on a pale neutral tabletop. Its case is ivory card over a graphite chassis, with a row of small frosted acrylic indicator lights across the front, one of them an acid-lime carrier light, dark and waiting. A single graphite phone line runs from its back in a neat gentle curve to a wall socket on a frosted glass panel. To the left, a graphite desk phone sits in its cradle; to the right, a cold mug and a small stack of ivory paper. Fine dust rests on the modem's vents.
end: The same modem is caught mid-retry. It has jolted a few millimetres off the desk from its own rattling, its frosted indicator lights flaring in a stuttering row, and the acid-lime carrier light is caught half lit, flickering. The phone line has whipped out of the wall socket and hangs mid-air in a loose loop, its plug swinging. The desk phone's handset has bounced out of its cradle and is mid-fall toward the floor. The paper stack beside the mug has fanned outward from the vibration, sheets sliding off the desk. Dust shakes from the vents in a thin cloud, and the socket plate is cracked.
apocalypse: A dusty scrubland of pale grey paper soil stretches toward low hills, crossed by a line of fallen graphite poles lying in the dust. At the centre, the modem sits half buried at the size of a warehouse, its ivory casing peeled and weathered, frosted lights cracked and dark. Its old phone line snakes across the plain toward the ruined frosted panel of the wall socket, but it is snapped in several places. A slim graphite cable-laying rig on thin wheels has been unspooling a new lime cable from a drum on its back, and it has just clicked the plug into the rebuilt socket, one link made.

title: Forecast board
hero: weather map board on a graphite easel
start: A weather map board about the size of a tea tray stands on a brushed graphite easel at the centre of a pale neutral tabletop. The map is ivory card with raised contour lines and softly embossed coastlines, with small graphite pressure-symbol pins placed across it. A single acid-lime front line, a thin raised strip, curves across the map. Above the easel on a slim graphite shelf, a frosted glass jar of small beads and a stack of ivory paper sit squared. A cold mug and a graphite pointer rest on a stool beside the board. Dust lies faint on the easel feet.
end: The forecast was wrong. A gust has blasted through the scene from the left, knocking the frosted glass jar off the shelf; it is mid-fall, spilling a hail of frosted beads that strike the board in a spray. The paper stack has lifted and sheets are slapping into the map. The acid-lime front line has torn half free and curls away from the card. Pressure pins have popped loose and fly outward. The easel has tipped back on two legs, and the stool is knocked over, the mug mid-roll across the tabletop. Beads bounce everywhere, all tracing back to the broken jar.
apocalypse: A storm-battered coastal headland of layered ivory card rock juts into a grey sea of frosted glass beads under a heavy sky. On the headland, the easel stands at the size of a lighthouse frame, legs bent and one snapped, with the map board torn and split, its contour lines bleached and its pins broken off. Drifts of beads have packed against the cliff and scattered across the rock. A slim graphite mast rig has bolted a new section of frame to the top of the easel, and on it a lime weather vane turns, now pointing steady into the wind.

title: Synergy merger
hero: two office models with org-chart blocks
start: Two small office building models stand side by side on a pale neutral tabletop, each about the height of a coffee cup. The left is brushed graphite, the right frosted acrylic, and both have a flat roof where a tidy org chart of ivory card blocks stands in stacked tiers, joined by thin graphite rods. The left chart is capped by a single acid-lime block at its peak. Between the buildings is a narrow gap. In the foreground, a folded ivory merger memo rests squared beside a graphite desk stamp. Dust lies faint along the roof edges.
end: The two buildings have been shoved together until their walls grind and the gap is gone. Their roof charts have merged in a crush: tiers overlap, rods snap, and duplicate ivory blocks are ejected, frozen mid-flight off both sides and tumbling toward the table. The acid-lime capstone has been knocked sideways and teeters on a jumbled pile of blocks. The frosted acrylic facade is cracked where the buildings meet. The merger memo has been scattered by falling blocks, and the stamp has tipped over. Dust spurts from the seam in a thin plume.
apocalypse: A long fault ridge crosses a wide pale plain where two landmasses have been pushed together, their edges buckled upward into a broken crest. On the crest stand the two office buildings fused at vast scale, graphite and frosted acrylic jammed together and cracked along the seam. Ejected org blocks lie scattered down both slopes like fallen boulders, weathered and bleached. A slim graphite alignment frame with lime rails stands on the crest and has stacked one clean column of blocks inside it, each block squared on the one below, rebuilding one chart.
